title: Just-open streak
intro: Opening the app before your chosen hour is a streak of its own.

title: If-then plans
intro: Decide in advance. The app reminds you at the time you pick, with a Start button.

title: Habit stacking
intro: Attach a session to something you already do every day, like morning tea or the college bus.

title: Temptation bundling
intro: Save a link to a favourite playlist. The play button shows only on the running timer, so the music belongs to work.

title: Start ritual
body: Sound, one breath, tap.

title: Ugly first draft
intro: Perfectionism cannot survive this goal.
task: Make it bad on purpose. Ugly counts.

title: Setup-only session
intro: No work required. Only get ready to work.
task: Open the files and clear the desk. Nothing else.

title: Dice start
intro: Cannot choose? Let the dice pick among up to three of your tasks.

title: Bad-day bar
intro: Rough day? Drop today's door to one minute. One minute still counts as a full win and keeps every streak.
setLabel: Today is a rough day: 1 minute is enough

title: Home-screen widget
body: Long-press your home screen, choose Widgets, find Challenger Timer and drop "Start 2 min" anywhere. It shows your streak and starts a session without opening the app. It turns from red to green once you have worked today.

title: Quick-settings tile
body: Pull down the notification shade twice, tap the pencil, and drag "Start 2 min" into your tiles. One tap there starts a session.

title: Voice start
body: On the Timer tab, tap the microphone and say "Start five minutes on DSA". It understands a number of minutes and a project name. Needs the phone's speech recogniser.

title: NFC desk tag
body: Write the link challengertimer://start to an NFC sticker with any free NFC writer app, and stick it on your desk. Tapping the phone on it starts a 2-minute session.

title: Arrived at my study place
intro: Automatic location detection is not built. This is the manual version: tap when you sit down at the library, lab or desk.
task: I just sat down. Open the first thing.

title: Charger cue
intro: Plugging the phone in offers a start. Android only allows this while the app is still alive in the background, so it will not fire if the app was closed long ago.
setLabel: Offer a start when I plug in

title: Morning first win
intro: Blocks every app (except phone, launcher and settings) until today's first session is finished. Needs Earn your phone switched on in Settings.
setLabel: Block all apps until the first session

title: Start count
intro: Also shown as the biggest number on Home.

title: Full and tiny versions
body: On the Streaks tab, tap a habit's name and give it a tiny version, like "Read one line". On a bad day the TINY button keeps the streak alive.

title: Weekly streaks
body: Some habits do not need to be daily. Tap a habit's name on the Streaks tab and choose "4 of 7 days". Its streak then counts weeks that hit the target.

title: Chain calendar
intro: This month. Every day you showed up is crossed off. A snowflake is a day a freeze covered.

title: Wake-time streak
intro: Tap the button when you get up. It counts if you are up no later than 30 minutes after your target.

title: Phone-free first hour
intro: Self-reported: tick it on days your first waking hour had no phone.

title: Review streak
intro: Counts days you answered the three daily questions (in the Reflection tools).

title: Hard-thing-first streak
intro: Self-reported: tick it on days you did the task you dreaded most before anything else.

title: Stacking bonus
body: Feed three streaks on the same day (for example a session plus two habit ticks) and that day pays an extra 30 XP.

title: Streak wager
intro: Bet some XP that the next 7 days pass without an uncovered miss. Freezes still protect you. Win: you gain the amount. Miss a day with no freeze: you lose it.

title: Active days
intro: Choose days that never count against any streak, for example Sunday. Work on those days still counts.

title: Time-window streaks
body: Tap a habit's name on the Streaks tab and set a window, like 06:00 to 09:00. The habit can then only be ticked inside it.

title: Graduation
body: When a habit runs on its own, tap its name on the Streaks tab and graduate it. It moves to "Maintained" and frees your attention for a new one.

title: Three daily questions
intro: Two minutes in the evening.

title: Earned freezes
body: Every 7 active days in a row earns one extra freeze. Earned freezes do not expire at month end. They show as extra lives on the Streaks tab.

title: Decay, not reset
intro: With this on, a break (two uncovered misses in a row) costs 20% of the streak instead of all of it. Off keeps the standard rule.
setLabel: A break keeps 80% of the streak

title: Comeback bonus
body: The first session after an uncovered miss pays its XP twice. Coming back is rewarded more than never slipping.

title: Repair task
intro: Missed yesterday? Do double the minimum today (4 minutes) and restore it.

title: Sick and travel mode
intro: Pauses every streak. No day counts as a miss while it is on. Use it when you are ill or travelling, not when you are avoiding.

title: Exam mode
intro: During exams, show only the habits you marked as your exam set (open a habit on the Streaks tab to mark it). The others are paused, not broken.

title: Miss autopsy
intro: One tap. No essay, no blame. It only feeds the pattern finder.

title: Fresh-start dates
intro: Mondays, the 1st of a month and your birthday are natural restart days. Home mentions it on those days if the streak needs a restart.

title: Lapse plan
intro: Write it now, while you are calm. Home shows it back to you right after a missed day.
prompts: If I miss a day, I will...

title: Friend test
intro: You are kinder to friends than to yourself. Borrow that.
prompts: What would I say to a friend who missed a day?

title: Archive
intro: Old habits are never deleted. Their streaks stay as proof you can do it.

title: Mood check
intro: One tap. Low-mood days you still worked on turn gold in the heatmap.

title: Pomodoro cycles
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and choose Pomodoro. Four 25-minute rounds with 5-minute breaks run by themselves while the app is open. All rounds share one proof at the end.

title: Flowtime
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and choose Flowtime. The timer counts up. Stop when focus fades and you are offered a break one fifth as long as the work.

title: Ramp ladder
intro: The Home session grows by one minute for each day you work, from 2 up to 60. Switch it off any time to go back to 2 minutes.
setLabel: Grow my daily session by 1 minute a day

title: Hard mode
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and switch on Hard mode before you start. If you leave the app for more than 10 seconds, that session ends without credit. Turning the screen off does not count as leaving.

title: Wander tally
intro: The running timer has a "mind wandered" button.

title: Strict breaks
intro: Breaks end on time. If you come back late, the overrun is counted here.

title: Ambient sounds
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and pick brown noise, a rain-like hiss or white noise. They are generated on the phone, so there is no cafe recording.

title: Marathon day
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and choose Marathon day: six 25-minute rounds with enforced 5-minute breaks. Optional, and only on days you choose.

title: Deadline tools
body: On the Plan tab, open a task (the arrow on its right), give it a due date and a rough size. The app then sets your own due date 48 hours early and shows sessions left, a daily quota, a start-by date, a backward plan, what waiting 5 days would cost, and the XP bonus for working early.

title: First-touch rule
intro: Every new task with a due date deserves 5 minutes within 24 hours. Open the task from the Plan tab to do it.

title: Neck-level alarm
intro: You also get one reminder a day at cue time while any deadline is at neck level.

title: Cost-of-delay note
intro: Write what the last all-nighter really cost you. It is shown back to you when you try to postpone a task.
prompts: What did the last-minute rush cost me?

title: Future-self letter
intro: Write as you, on the morning after the deadline, to you now.
prompts: Dear me, it is the morning after. Here is what I wish you would do today:

title: Load calendar
intro: The next 8 weeks by how much is due. Three or more due dates in one week are flagged.

title: Deadline post-mortem
intro: Three lines after each deadline. No judgement, only data for next time.

title: Camera-first capture
intro: Open the proof screen on the camera option, so a notebook page is one tap away.

title: Daily page
intro: Today, assembled.

title: Weekly digest
intro: This week in six lines, ready to share.

title: Done list
intro: The opposite of a to-do list: things that are finished.

title: Evidence wall
intro: Proof that I can do hard things.

title: Portfolio export
intro: Your pinned items as a text block for a resume or portfolio.

title: Share card
intro: A picture sized for a WhatsApp status.

title: Progress photos
intro: One photo a week for long projects. Small changes become visible.

title: Small wins journal
intro: Three small wins. Small on purpose.

title: One Big Thing
intro: One must-do for today. Only one.

title: 1-3-5 list
intro: One big, three medium, five small. Nothing more fits in a day.

title: Someday shelf
intro: Ideas that are not for now. Parked, not lost.

title: Stuck button
intro: Stuck is information, not failure. Pick one way out and note what the block was.
prompts: What exactly am I stuck on?

title: Templates
intro: A ready project with small first steps.

title: Project retro
intro: Three questions when a project ends.

title: Evening plan
intro: Three minutes tonight saves the argument tomorrow.
items: Set tomorrow's first task on the Plan tab
Put what I need on the desk

title: Time blocks
intro: Put a task on the clock. You get a reminder with a Start button at that time.

title: Big rocks first
intro: The three that matter go in before anything else.

title: Theme days
intro: Give days a theme, for example Saturday is project day.

title: Weekly review
intro: Ten minutes on Sunday.

title: Weekly targets
intro: Sessions per project per week.

title: WOOP
intro: Wish, outcome, obstacle, plan. Picturing the obstacle is what makes it work.
prompts: If that obstacle shows up, then I will

title: Obstacle pre-mortem
intro: Tomorrow has not gone wrong yet. Guess how it would.
prompts: What I will do about it now

title: Shutdown ritual
intro: End the work day on purpose.

title: Commute list
intro: Small tasks for the bus.
prompts: A task I can do on the bus

title: Dead-time list
intro: Five-minute tasks for gaps.

title: 12-week goals
intro: A quarter is short enough to feel. A year is not.
prompts: How I will know it is done
Weekly action that gets me there

title: Inputs over outcomes
body: You cannot do "get good marks". You can do "one session". This app counts only the inputs you control: starts, sessions, proof. Marks follow those with a delay.

title: App blocker in sessions
intro: Your blocked apps (chosen in Settings) are also blocked while a session is running. Needs usage access and display-over-apps, like Earn your phone.
setLabel: Block my chosen apps during sessions

title: Allow-list
intro: Apps that stay open even in block-all mode. Phone, launcher and settings are always allowed.

title: Strict lock
intro: Hide the STOP button for the first minutes of every session. Android does not let an app stop you leaving, so pair this with the app blocker.
setLabel: No STOP for the first N minutes (0 = off)

title: Auto Do Not Disturb
intro: Switches Do Not Disturb on when a session starts and off when it ends. Calls from starred contacts still ring if your phone is set that way. Needs "Do Not Disturb access" in system settings.

title: Greyscale prompt
body: A grey phone is a boring phone. During work hours, turn on greyscale: Settings, Accessibility, Colour correction (or Digital Wellbeing, Bedtime mode). Android does not let an app flip this for you.

title: Face-down start
intro: With the app open, put the phone face down for two seconds and a 2-minute session starts.
setLabel: Start when I put the phone face down

title: Urge surfing
intro: Want to quit or scroll? Wait 90 seconds and breathe. The urge peaks and passes. Then choose.

title: Ten-minute rule
intro: Want Instagram? Allowed. After ten more minutes.
task: Ten more minutes, then I may choose.

title: Parking lot
intro: Jot the distracting thought here and go back to work. It will still be here.

title: Unlock friction
intro: Adds an "open it anyway" button to the block screen that makes you wait 10 seconds, then lets that app through for 5 minutes.
setLabel: Allow opening a blocked app after a 10-second wait

title: Scheduled scroll time
body: Pick an hour below. For 30 minutes from that hour the blocker stands down, guilt-free, every day. Choosing 0 switches it off.

title: Time-thief report
intro: The three apps that took the most of today.

title: Website blocker
body: Not part of this app. A desktop browser extension is a separate program that would have to be built and installed on your computer.

title: Single-tab pledge
items: One tab for this session. I close the rest now.

title: Attention warm-up
intro: Sixty seconds of slow breathing before hard work.

title: Message batching
intro: Two reminders a day, at 1 pm and 7 pm, to check messages then and not in between.
setLabel: Remind me at my two message times

title: Night lock
intro: A nudge to put screens down at the hour you choose.

title: No pay-to-win
body: There is nothing to buy in this app, with money or with coins, that skips the work. XP, rank and streaks come only from sessions, proof and habits.

title: Identity statement
intro: Shown on the running timer every session.

title: Belief check
intro: Write the old belief. Then read what your own logs say back.
prompts: The old belief (for example: I never finish)

title: "Not yet" wording
body: Nothing in this app is called failed. Unfinished things are "not yet". If you ever find the word failed on a screen, that is a bug.

title: Hard-things ladder
intro: A record of the hardest things you have done. Read it on bad days.

title: Future-self card
intro: You in five years, in your own words.

title: Letter to self
intro: Write now. Open it again in 30 days: each entry shows its date.

title: Values pick
intro: Three values. When a task feels pointless, check which one it serves.

title: Why chain
intro: Ask why five times about your main goal.

title: Anti-vision
intro: One paragraph on the life you get by drifting. Open it only when you choose to.
prompts: If I keep drifting, in five years...

title: Vision card
intro: The role you are aiming at, concretely.
prompts: What a normal day looks like

title: Role-model board
intro: One principle each from people you admire.
prompts: The one principle I take from them

title: Personal rules
intro: For example: I never skip Monday.

title: Start mantra
intro: A line of your own for the moment before you start.

title: Name talk
body: When you have not started yet, Home speaks to you by name, in the third person: "Winzo, start the timer." Talking to yourself by name creates a little distance from the feeling.

title: Effort praise
body: The app praises what you did, never what you are. "You started" is in your control. "You are smart" is not.

title: Standards page
intro: The daily minimum you refuse to go below.
prompts: My floor, even on the worst day

title: Reframe library
body:
"I do not feel like it." You do not need to. Two minutes needs no mood.

"It is too late today." The day ends at 3 am. Two minutes still fits.

"I will do double tomorrow." Tomorrow-you says the same. Do a single today.

"I do not know where to start." Then the task is: write down where to start.

"It has to be good." It has to exist. Good comes from editing.

title: Excuse log
intro: Write the excuse, then answer it as you would answer a friend.

title: Effort rating
intro: Proofs can be tagged tired, bored or scared on the proof screen.

title: Personal constitution
intro: One page, written and signed by you.

title: Yearly identity review
intro: Once a year.
prompts: Who was I a year ago?
Who do I want to be next year?

title: Name the feeling
intro: Naming a feeling takes some of its force away. Tap the closest one and get a matching way in.

title: Explainer card
body: Procrastination is not laziness. It is how the mind escapes a bad feeling about a task: boredom, fear, confusion. So shouting at yourself makes it worse, and shrinking the task makes it better. That is why everything here starts at two minutes.

title: Aversion type
intro: What is it about this task? Each kind has its own fix.

title: Worry dump
intro: Two minutes of writing every worry down before starting. They are easier to carry on paper.

title: Box breathing
intro: In for four, hold four, out four, hold four. One minute.

title: "Good enough" line
body: Open a task from the Plan tab and tap DEFINE "GOOD ENOUGH". One sentence on what done looks like stops perfectionism from moving the finish line.

title: Fear-setting
intro: Name the fear and it shrinks to its real size.

title: Shame-free language
body: A rule for every screen, alarm and message in this app: no blame, no insult, no guilt. A tested rule: the buddy message, the Home line and the break ideas are checked for it automatically.

title: Overwhelm mode
intro: Hides everything on Home except the next step and one button.

title: Action-first card
body: Motivation usually shows up after you start, not before. Waiting to feel like it is waiting for the effect before the cause.

title: Mood after
intro: One tap when a session ends.

title: Trigger log
intro: What you did instead. No judgement, only data.

title: Replacement plan
intro: One rule for your most common escape.
prompts: If I want to open ___, I first do one 2-minute session

title: Company prompt
body: Been working alone for a long while? Sit beside someone who is also working: a friend, the library, a study room. You do not have to talk.

title: Stress meter
intro: Once a week. A high rating makes the app ask for less, not more.

title: Gratitude line
intro: One sentence a day.

title: Instant celebration
body: The moment a session ends the screen flips, the phone buzzes, a tone plays and you are told to fist pump. Celebrating right away is what wires a habit in.

title: Sleep log
intro: Hours last night.

title: Wind-down alarm
intro: A reminder 45 minutes before your bedtime.

title: Protected sleep window
body: Between your bedtime and wake time (set in Wind-down alarm and Morning light) the app schedules no reminders at all, and no challenge can override that.

title: Energy check
intro: Morning, afternoon, evening.

title: Morning or night type
body: Pick the hour you naturally come alive. It becomes your suggested cue time in Settings.

title: Morning light reminder
intro: Ten minutes outside after waking.

title: Movement break
body: In sessions of 50 minutes or more, the running timer tells you to stand up and move at each 50-minute mark.

title: Walk session
intro: A walk is recovery, not a break from being productive.

title: Exercise streak
intro: The minimum is five. More is allowed.

title: Meal log
intro: Tap when you eat. Work days with fewer than two meals are worth noticing.

title: Caffeine cut-off
intro: A reminder at 3 pm.

title: Nap timer
intro: Twenty minutes. Longer leaves you groggy.

title: Eye rest
body: Every 20 minutes of a running session, the timer asks you to look far away for 20 seconds.

title: Posture ping
body: Every 30 minutes of a running session, the timer asks for a posture check.

title: 90/20 mode
body: On the Timer tab, "More ways to run it" has 90/20: ninety minutes of work, twenty of rest, twice.

title: Planned rest day
body: Use Active days (in the streak tools) to mark one weekday as rest. It never counts against a streak.

title: Active rest menu
body: Walk. Stretch. Music with your eyes closed. Talk to a friend, out loud, not by text. Rest that is not a screen.

title: Basics check
intro: Confirm these before any sprint or marathon day.

title: Boredom training
intro: Five minutes with nothing: no phone, no music. Sit. It builds the tolerance that study needs.
task: Sit with nothing for five minutes.

title: Buddy pairing
body: One buddy is saved in Settings and gets your daily result by SMS. A two-way pairing, where you also see their result inside the app, needs a server (BACKEND.md).

title: Shared session room
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Fail-together mode
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Who is working now
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Body doubling
intro: Save a video-call link (Meet, Zoom, Jitsi) you and a friend use to work side by side. Open it from here before you start.

title: Class squad
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Squad streak
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Consistency leaderboard
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Seven-day duel
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Commitment contract
intro: A promise in your own words, sent to a real person.
body: Commitment from {name}: I promise to {0} by {1}. If I miss, I will {2}. Please hold me to it.

title: Small money stake
intro: Optional. The app records the stake and does not move any money: paying is between you and your friend or the charity.
prompts: Paid to (friend or charity) if I miss

title: Forfeit
intro: Ask your buddy to choose a harmless penalty for a missed week.
body: {name} here. My target this week: {0}. If I miss it, you pick a harmless forfeit for me. What will it be?

title: Buddy-verified proof
intro: Send what you did to your buddy and ask for a thumbs up. The app cannot record their reply without a server.
body: Proof from {name}: {0}. Today: {today} sessions, {minutes} min. Does this count? Reply yes or no.

title: Mentor view
intro: Send your week to a senior or teacher. They see it only when you send it.
body: Weekly update from {name}: streak {streak} days, {starts} starts so far, rank {rank}. {0}

title: Family report
intro: An optional weekly summary for home.
body: This week from {name}: showing up {streak} days in a row. {0}

title: Public pledge card
intro: Say it where people can see it.
body: I pledge: {0}. Day {streak} of showing up. Ask me about it.

title: Build in public
intro: A draft of today's progress post. Edit before posting.
body: Day {streak}: {0}. {today} sessions, {minutes} minutes. Next: {step}

title: Cheers
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Help request
intro: Stuck? Ask a person. Through the share sheet for now: a squad feed needs a server.
body: Stuck on: {0}. Tried: {1}. Ten minutes of your help would unblock me.

title: Teaching credit
intro: Explaining a topic to someone counts as a session. Proof afterwards: what you explained.
task: Explain one topic to a buddy, out loud.

title: Check-in call scheduler
intro: A fixed time to call your buddy, with a reminder.

title: Group deadline board
intro: A local list for your team's due dates. Teammates do not see it without a server.

title: Team roles
intro: Who owns what in a group project.

title: Privacy controls
body: Nothing is shared by itself except one thing you switch on: the 8 pm buddy SMS, which carries sessions, minutes and streak. Everything else (digest, pledge, proof) leaves the phone only when you tap SHARE and choose who gets it. Per-person visibility rules need a server.

title: Five-minute blocks
intro: Plan a stretch of the day in very small blocks. Each block gets a reminder.

title: First-principles card
intro: Break it down to what is certainly true, then rebuild.
prompts: What I know is certainly true

title: Sprint week
body: One week of long hours, sleep untouched, then a lighter week. Before starting, pass the Basics check. Use Marathon day or 90/20 on the Timer tab for the long blocks. The app does not raise any target for you, and never schedules inside your sleep window.

title: Intensity dial
body: Pick this week's gear. It is a note to yourself: the app keeps asking for two minutes either way.

title: Regret test
prompts: At 80, will I regret skipping this?
So what do I do today?

title: 25/5 list
intro: Write 25 goals. Keep 5. The other 20 are the ones to avoid, because they are tempting.
prompts: What I will do to avoid the other 20

title: Franklin's two questions
prompts: Morning: what good shall I do today?
Evening: what good have I done today?

title: Virtue of the week
intro: Name the trait in the habit title if you like, and tick it each day you practised it.

title: Early session badge
body: Start a session before 8 am to earn "Before The Bell". Twenty of them earn "Dawn Shift".

title: Deliberate practice
intro: Work at the edge of what you can do, and check each attempt straight away.
task: One hard problem type. Attempt, check, fix, repeat.

title: Deep work blocks
body: Mark a session as DEEP WORK on the Timer tab and use a 50 or 90 minute preset. Switch on app blocking in sessions and auto Do Not Disturb to protect it.

title: One percent better
prompts: One small thing I improved today

title: Six-task list
intro: Six tasks, ranked. Do them in order. Unfinished ones move to tomorrow's list.

title: Shorter boxes
intro: Work fills the time you give it. Give this one less.
task: Finish a rough version in 15 minutes.

title: Stoic morning
prompts: What could get in my way today?

title: Inversion
prompts: How would I guarantee failure at this?

title: Hamming question
prompts: The most important problem in my field
Why I am not working on it

title: Build and sell
intro: Track both making things and showing them.

title: Pain log
intro: Pain plus reflection.

title: Say-no list
intro: What you turned down this week to protect your focus.

title: Maker's schedule
body: Guard one half-day with nothing booked in it. On the Timer tab, 90/20 gives two long uninterrupted rounds for it.

title: Ask for criticism
intro: Once a week, ask someone for honest feedback on your work.

title: Skill gap map
prompts: Next step to close the gap

title: Skill roadmaps
intro: Milestones for the skill you are building. Tick them off.

title: Problem count
intro: Entered by hand. Syncing from coding sites needs their APIs (BACKEND.md).

title: Pattern tracker
intro: Problem types you have covered: two pointers, sliding window, BFS...
prompts: A pattern I can now solve

title: Ship monthly
intro: One finished project every month.

title: Commit mirror
body: Not connected. This needs a server that both phones talk to (see BACKEND.md). Until one exists the app shows nothing here: no made-up people, no made-up numbers.

title: Competition log
prompts: What I built or my rank

title: Maths track
intro: Linear algebra, probability, statistics: topics as you finish them.

title: Mock interviews
intro: Run it timed (use a 50-minute session), then score yourself.

title: Speaking reps
intro: Five minutes of speaking English out loud. Save a voice note as proof.
task: Speak in English about today's work for five minutes.

title: Living resume
intro: Built from the items you pinned in the Vault.

title: Networking streak
habit: One message to a senior or professional

title: One-hour card
body: One hour a day is 365 hours a year. That is nine full work weeks, taken from nowhere but the evenings you would not remember anyway.

title: Teach-back posts
intro: Write up what you learned so someone else could learn it.

title: Yearly checkpoint
prompts: Where am I against the target role?

title: Syllabus tracker
intro: Units as a checklist. Name them like "OS: Unit 2".

title: Same-day revision
intro: Ten minutes on a lecture the day it happens saves an hour later.
task: Re-read today's lecture notes and mark what is unclear.

title: Spaced repetition
intro: Add what you learned as cards. They come back after 1, 3, 7 and 21 days.

title: Active recall
intro: Close the book. Write everything you remember. Then check.
task: Book closed: write what I remember.

title: Blurting
intro: Dump everything you know on one topic on a blank page, then mark the gaps.
task: Blurt one topic, then check the gaps.

title: Past-paper timer
intro: Run it as a 90-minute session in hard mode, then log the mark.

title: Exam plan generator
intro: Units spread evenly over the days you have.

title: Weak-topic list
prompts: A topic I keep getting wrong

title: Error log
intro: A notebook of mistakes and fixes.

title: Assignment and lab-record tracker
body: Add each assignment or lab record as a task on the Plan tab and give it a due date. The task screen then tracks it with all the deadline tools.

title: Attendance tracker
intro: Tick present or absent after each class.

title: Doubt list
intro: Questions to ask the teacher.

title: Interleaving
body: In one study block, switch subject every 25 minutes: use Pomodoro on the Timer tab and pick a different project each round. Mixing feels harder and sticks better.

title: Viva cards
intro: Likely questions with short answers. For timed review, add them as flashcards too.

title: Notes scanner
body: Take a photo of your notes as proof at the end of a session (PHOTO on the proof screen). It lands in the Vault under that project. There is no page-edge detection or PDF.

title: Group study session
body: Not connected. A timer shared across phones needs a server (BACKEND.md). Until then: start the same preset together and compare receipts.

title: Backlog plan
intro: Clear missed units in dated steps. Add each step as a task with a due date for reminders.

title: Committee bucket
intro: Cap the hours you give to committee and magazine work, so it cannot eat study time. Track it as its own project and compare in Subject balance.

title: Weekly experiment
intro: Test one change for a week.

title: Coach summary
intro: The AI coach is not connected (BACKEND.md). These lines are computed on the phone from your own log, with fixed rules. Nothing is guessed.

title: One smart reminder
body: Your cue alarm is the one reminder that matters. Its time is set in Settings and each evening on the Plan tab.

title: Your own words
intro: The cue alarm's headline, written by you.

title: Escalation ladder
body: Three steps, and that is all: the cue alarm at your time, one gentle nudge 30 minutes later if you have not started, and the 9 pm rescue.

title: Daily cap
body: Ordinary reminders stop after this many in a day. The cue alarm and the 9 pm rescue are separate and always ring.

title: Quiet hours
body: No ordinary reminders between these hours. Pick the same hour twice to switch it off.

title: Streak-at-risk alert
body: At 6 pm, if the streak is alive and today is still open, one reminder with a Start button.

title: Morning brief
intro: One line after you wake: today's first step.

title: Evening wrap
intro: One line at 9:30 pm: what today held.

title: Night-before reminder
body: At 9 pm, only if tomorrow has no first task yet.

title: Start-by reminders
body: A reminder on the day a task must start to finish calmly, not on the day it is due.

title: Humour voice
body: Dry and a little funny, never at your expense. The rank names are the proof.

title: Tone picker
body: Choose the voice of the line on Home before you start. 1 coach, 2 friend, 3 drill sergeant, 4 monk. None of them is allowed to blame you.

title: No-guilt rule
body: No message may blame or shame. It is enforced by tests on the buddy message, the Home line and the support text.

title: Celebration alerts
body: Milestones and comebacks are celebrated inside the app the moment they happen: the DONE screen, badges and bonus XP. There is no separate notification for them.

title: Notes from past you
intro: Write encouraging lines to yourself. One comes back as a notification at 4 pm each day.
prompts: A line future me should hear

title: Buddy nudges
body: Not connected. A nudge from your buddy's phone to yours needs a server (BACKEND.md).

title: Place reminders
body: Not built. Reminders triggered by arriving somewhere need background location, which this app does not ask for. Closest version: "Arrived at my study place" in the toolbox, tapped by hand.

title: Class silence
body: Reminders that would ring during a lecture on your Timetable are dropped for that day.

title: Costly snooze
body: The alarm has no snooze button. To delay, you have to open Settings and pick an exact new cue time.

title: Sunday preview
body: On Sunday at 6 pm, one message with how many due dates the week holds.

title: Fatigue monitor
body: Not automatic yet. If you notice you are ignoring the alarm, change its time or its words (Your own words) so it is new again.

title: Languages
body: 1 English, 2 Hindi, 3 Marathi. Only the main words on Home and the timer are translated so far. Everything else stays in English.

title: Accessibility
body: Text size for the whole app, on top of your phone's own font setting. Buttons are at least 48 dp tall and text is white or cyan on black.

title: Dogfood rule
body: Building something? Make it a project here and log every work session on it with proof. The app that built habits should be built by habit.

title: One goal question
prompts: The single thing I most want to stop delaying

title: One habit only
body: During your first seven days the app asks you to stay with one habit. You can still add another if you insist.

title: Delay quiz
intro: Five questions. Your answers are kept for you to reread: they do not change settings by themselves.
prompts: When in the day do I delay most?
Which kind of task do I delay most?
What feeling comes just before I delay?
What has worked for me before?

title: Just-in-time tips
body: Tools appear in the Toolbox as your rank rises, and the Toolbox shows which ones unlock next. Nothing is explained before you can use it.

title: Sample day
body: EXAMPLE, not your data. 7:30 alarm shows "Open notebook to page 12". Tap Start 2 min. Timer ends, you type one line of proof and a parking note. Evening: set tomorrow's first task. 8 pm: your buddy gets one SMS. That is a whole good day.

title: Task import
body: Paste a list of tasks into the Task splitter tool: each line becomes a task. Import from Google Tasks is not connected (BACKEND.md).

title: Calendar connect
body: Not built. Reading your phone calendar would need the calendar permission. Use the Timetable tool to enter your classes by hand.

title: Tone at setup
body: Pick the voice in the Tone picker tool. It is not part of the first-run setup, to keep that under a minute.

title: Student starter pack
intro: Three small habits for college.

title: Fading support
body: In your first week up to three ordinary reminders a day may ring. After that the limit drops to two unless you set your own in Daily cap.

title: Day-3 dip message
body: On day three and four, Home tells you that the dip in motivation is normal.

title: Week-two choice
body: From day eight you can add a second habit on the Streaks tab, or stay with one. Staying with one is a fine choice.

title: Coach chat
body: The AI version is not connected (BACKEND.md). No chat is shown, because a fake one would have to make things up. The Coach tools below answer from your own log with fixed rules.

title: Task rewriter
intro: Turns "study ML" into a physical first action, using fixed patterns.

title: Time estimates
intro: Suggested from your own finished tasks.

title: Stuck helper
body: The AI version is not connected (BACKEND.md). Use the Stuck button and the Feeling tools: they give a first step for each kind of block.

title: Notes Q&A
body: The AI version is not connected (BACKEND.md). Nothing is shown.

title: Quiz maker
body: The AI version is not connected (BACKEND.md). Flashcards quiz you on what you typed in yourself.

title: Auto daily log
body: The Daily page tool assembles the day's sessions, proof and notes by itself.

title: Auto-tagging
body: Proof inherits the project and tag of its session automatically. Sorting by subject from the content of a photo is not connected (BACKEND.md).

title: Photo to text
body: Not connected. Reading handwriting needs an OCR library or service (BACKEND.md). Photos stay photos.

title: Voice journal
intro: Speak and the phone's speech recogniser turns it into a text entry.

title: Auto-reschedule
body: Not automatic. A missed task is moved with the "Move to tomorrow" button on its screen, which also counts the move.

title: Deadline extraction
intro: Paste a notice. If it holds a date, it becomes a task with that due date.

title: Resume bullet writer
body: The AI version is not connected (BACKEND.md). The Living resume tool lists your pinned proof as plain bullets.

title: Roadmap generator
body: The AI version is not connected (BACKEND.md). Write your own milestones in Skill roadmaps.

title: Off switch
body: Every coach tool has its own switch in Settings, Features. All of them compute from your own log with fixed rules and say so when there is not enough data.

title: Morning routine builder
intro: Add the steps in order, then run them one at a time.

title: Pack the bag
habit: Pack the bag the night before

title: Desk reset
habit: Clear the desk after the last session

title: Three quiet minutes
intro: Sit and breathe for three minutes.

title: Message check times
habit: Checked messages only at my two times

title: Chore tracker
intro: Chores with whose turn it is.

title: Errand batch
intro: One weekly slot for laundry and shopping.

title: Digital cleanup
habit: Sorted files and downloads this week

title: One-tap routine run
body: Open the Morning or Night routine builder and tap RUN: the steps play one at a time.

title: Routine timer
body: Each routine run is timed. The builder shows your best time to beat.

title: Anchor moments
intro: Three fixed slots to hang habits on.

title: Two-minute rule
body: If it takes under two minutes, do it now. Not later, not on a list. Now.

title: Daily non-negotiables
intro: Three at most. If you have more than three, none of them is non-negotiable.

title: Monthly theme
body: The monthly campaign changes name each month. The colours of the app do not change.

title: Rotating challenge types
body: The daily challenge cycles through five different kinds, so two days in a row never ask for the same thing.

title: Planned reward fade
body: Not built as an automatic fade. When a habit runs by itself, graduate it (Streaks tab) so it stops asking for attention.

title: Monthly goal reset
prompts: What I am dropping to make room

title: Auto difficulty
body: The weekly boss already adjusts: it asks for one more session than you did last week, and never less than five.

title: Plateau note
body: Flat weeks are normal. Skill grows in steps, not in a line: weeks of nothing visible, then a jump. Keep the daily start and wait for the step.

title: Anniversary badges
body: One year and two years after your first day, a badge appears on Me.

title: Dormant mode
body: After days away, Home shrinks to one button and hides every number until you have started again.

title: Short re-onboarding
body: Coming back is one screen: Start again. Your habits, projects and vault are as you left them.

title: Simple mode
body: Me, Settings, Simple mode hides everything except Start, timer, proof, streaks and plan.

title: Custom home
body: Home is kept to one button on purpose. You can switch off the start count (feature 23) and the bonus bar in Settings.

title: Seasonal events
body: Exam season: switch on Exam mode. Summer build season: start a project from the Hackathon template and use Ship monthly.

title: New-semester reset
items: Add this semester's subjects as projects
Set the cue time for the new schedule

title: Guide a junior
intro: Help someone else start.
body: {0}, try this with me: two minutes of work a day, with proof. I am on day {streak}. I will check on you tomorrow.

title: Idea box
intro: Improvements for this app as you use it.

title: Builder's changelog
intro: Each release you ship is an achievement.

title: Graduation test
intro: Turns every ordinary reminder off for seven days. The cue alarm and rescue stay under their own switches in Settings.

title: Daily deposit
body: With the dial on Firm, the day's 100 points drain evenly from the start of the day until your first session starts. Start at noon and you keep about 60. The Home bonus bar shows the drain.

title: Melting block
body: A block of ice on Home shrinks through the day until you start. It comes back whole each morning.

title: Invested-hours counter
body: When you try to stop a session early, the dialog shows the hours you have already put into that project.

title: Album with gaps
intro: One square per day this month. Days you showed up are filled. A missed day stays blank unless you repair it the next day.

title: Cracking bricks
body: In the Workshop builder, bricks show cracks after idle days. One session repairs them.

title: Theme on loan
body: Not built. The app has one look, so there is no favourite theme to lend and take back.

title: Weekly escrow
intro: Record an amount you set aside with a person you trust, to be handed back session by session. The app only keeps the tally: it holds no money.

title: Refundable 21-day deposit
intro: Record a deposit held by someone you trust, returned if you never miss twice in a row for 21 days. The app only records it.

title: Disliked-cause stake
intro: Record a stake that goes to a cause you would rather not fund if you miss. The app does not collect or send money.

title: Expiring coins
body: With the dial on Firm, your coins are frozen at zero after 7 idle days and return the day you do a session.

title: Falling multiplier
body: With the dial on Firm, the first start of the day pays up to 3 times its XP right after your wake hour, dropping a quarter each hour to normal.

title: Half-built display
intro: Half-done tasks stay listed here until they are finished.

title: Name it
intro: Named things are harder to abandon.

title: Built by you
body: Everything at risk in this app is something you made: your habits, your plant's name, your promises, your vault. Nothing here was handed to you finished.

title: Demotion notice
body: After six idle days you get one reminder: the shown rank slips tomorrow unless a session happens.

title: Title swap
body: After three idle days, Home shows a funny stand-in title until your next session. It is a joke, not a verdict.

title: Paid insurance
intro: Spending coins on a freeze makes you value the streak it protects.

title: Lives display
body: Freezes are shown as hearts on the Streaks tab.

title: Foot in the door
body: The app only ever asks for two minutes. When they are done it offers "just five more", once, and takes no for an answer.

title: Typed oath
intro: Type it each night. Tomorrow the app checks whether a session followed.

title: Signed plan
intro: Sign tomorrow's plan with your finger.

title: Your own voice
intro: Record your promise. It plays when the cue alarm opens.

title: Desk selfie
intro: A photo of you at your desk becomes the picture on tomorrow's alarm.

title: Consistency mirror
body: On some days, before you start, Home quotes your identity statement back: "You said you are someone who starts. Starting now keeps that true." Set the statement in Identity statement.

title: Yes ladder
intro: Three easy questions, then the real one.

title: Auto-start by default
intro: Relentless only. At cue time the 2-minute session starts by itself and the alarm tells you so. To cancel you have to stop it. It never fires inside your sleep window.
setLabel: Start my session at cue time unless I cancel

title: Cancel sentence
body: With the dial on Firm, stopping a session before two minutes means typing: I am choosing to skip my work today.

title: Skip delay
body: With the dial on Firm, stopping before two minutes has a 30-second wait first.

title: Honest buttons
body: With the dial on Firm, the early-stop button reads "I choose to delay my goal" instead of "Stop".

title: Ulysses lock
intro: Relentless only. Your blocked apps are locked every day between the hours below. Switching it off takes 24 hours.

title: Permission guard
body: If a permission the locks depend on is switched off, your buddy gets one SMS saying so. Needs the buddy report's SMS permission.

title: Booked sessions
intro: An appointment with yourself, with a reminder.

title: Timed vault
intro: Relentless only. For exam week.

title: Code with a buddy
body: Not built. An unlock code held by your buddy would let either of you bypass the 24-hour rule, so it needs a design with a server to be safe (BACKEND.md).

title: Reasons archive
body: When you try to stop early, the dialog shows the "why" line you wrote for that project.

title: Days-since-zero widget
intro: The home-screen widget shows days since a zero instead of the streak. Android does not allow widgets on the lock screen any more.
setLabel: Widget shows days since a zero

title: Wallpaper maker
intro: Save the card as an image, then set it as your wallpaper from your gallery.

title: Morning contract
body: The cue alarm is the contract: it shows the task you locked last night and one button. The app cannot hook the very first unlock of the day.

title: No choices
body: Home offers exactly one next step and one button. There is nothing to deliberate.

title: Live counter
body: Not connected. This needs a server that your buddy's or squad's phones also talk to (BACKEND.md). Nothing is shown, because any number here would have to be invented.

title: Session time-lapse
body: Not built. Recording video of a whole session needs the camera running in the background. Photo proof at the end is the supported version.

title: Desk check-in
intro: Take a photo as proof, then send a timestamped line to your people.
body: Desk check-in from {name}: at {0}, session {today} today, day {streak}.

title: Respected reader
intro: Send your week to a senior or teacher you look up to.
body: Weekly digest from {name}: {streak}-day streak, {starts} starts in total. {0}

title: Dedicated session
intro: Dedicate your next session to someone you care about, then start it from Home.

title: Status card
intro: Your streak as an image sized for a WhatsApp status.

title: Profile frames
body: From rank 9 upward the rank card on Me gets a gold frame.

title: 100-day club
body: The "Hundred Club" badge. The only way in is a 100-day streak.

title: Mystery box
body: Each session carries one hidden line. It appears on the running timer, never before you start.

title: Hidden line
body: Today's line shows only after two minutes of work.

title: Reward spin
body: Every saved proof spins for 5 to 25 XP. It shows under "Reward spins" in your XP breakdown on Me.

title: Rare drops
body: About one session in a hundred carries a legendary badge. You find out only by finishing it.

title: Sixty-minute quest
body: Today's double hour is the quest: it exists for one hour only, and a start inside it pays double.

title: Five-minute offer
body: Start a session within five minutes of opening the app and it pays 10 XP extra.

title: Ring left open
intro: Yesterday's ring closed at day end. This is today's, still open.

title: Puzzle pieces
intro: A picture uncovered one piece per session.

title: Fog map
intro: Each session clears one square of fog.

title: Completion sound
body: A short tone that plays only when a session, a proof or a habit is completed. Nowhere else.

title: Timer heartbeat
intro: A soft pulse every ten seconds while the timer runs.

title: Escalating flame
body: The streak flame on Home grows at 3, 7, 14, 30, 66 and 100 days.

title: Daily rotation
body: The daily challenge changes with the day. Yesterday's is gone.

title: Red dot
body: Switch on the Sticky banner: on most launchers its notification puts a dot on the app icon until your first session.

title: Sticky banner
intro: A "not started yet" notification that stays until today's first session.
setLabel: Keep a notice up until I start

title: Red-to-green widget
body: The home-screen widget's button is red until you have worked today, then green.

title: Wallpaper by day state
body: Not built. Replacing your phone wallpaper by itself is more than this app should do. The widget changes colour instead.

title: Start replaces scroll
body: Earn your phone does this: opening a blocked app before your first session shows a one-tap 2-minute start instead.

title: Two minutes, today
body: Open the app and start a 2-minute session every single day. If the app does only this for you, it has worked. Everything else exists to protect this.
